claims.claim: Merwin defines the opening scene as the answer to 'where am I' and the hook as the answer to 'why am I here'.
claims.source: Shawn Merwin, 'Let's Design an Adventure: Adventure Hooks and Opening Scenes', D&D Beyond, 2019
claims.quote: The “where” is the opening scene, and the “why” is the adventure hook
claims.page: section 'You May Ask Yourself, How Did I Get Here?'

claims.claim: Peterson reports Keep on the Borderlands selling 750,000 copies a year at the height of the 1981 boom.
claims.source: Jon Peterson, Game Wizards (MIT Press 2021), excerpt published by Polygon

claims.claim: A long-form reader writeup describes the D&D Gazetteer line's language as casual and informal.
claims.source: Rulebook Heavily, 'Dungeons & Dragons Gazetteer' writeup, RPG Writeups
claims.quote: The language is casual and informal

claims.claim: The writeup says GAZ1's chapter of place descriptions is meant mostly for players rather than the DM.
claims.source: Rulebook Heavily, 'Dungeons & Dragons Gazetteer' writeup, RPG Writeups
claims.quote: The descriptions in this chapter are mostly meant for players
claims.page: Gaz 1 Part 4: The Lay of the Land

claims.claim: The same essay characterises Gygax's prose as resembling a baroque sermon.
claims.source: Serban Ionita, 'The Shadowed Old Gods of Game Design', The RPG Gazette, 2025
claims.quote: whose prose resembled a baroque sermon

claims.claim: Deterding and Zagal place the study of textuality, authorship and narrative in RPGs with literary and media scholars in the 2000s.
claims.source: Sebastian Deterding and Jose P. Zagal, 'The Many Faces of Role-Playing Game Studies', in Role-Playing Game Studies (Routledge 2018)
claims.quote: textuality, authorship, and narrative in RPGs
claims.page: section on the history of RPG studies

claims.claim: Deterding and Zagal credit Peterson and Appelcline, independent authors, with the substantial historiographies of tabletop role-playing games.
claims.source: Sebastian Deterding and Jose P. Zagal, 'The Many Faces of Role-Playing Game Studies', in Role-Playing Game Studies (Routledge 2018)
claims.quote: have produced substantial historiographies of the emergence and evolution
claims.page: section on the history of RPG studies

claims.claim: Baur says the most important thing to know about world building is who you are doing it for.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 1, 2025
claims.quote: the most important thing to know about world building is, who

claims.claim: Cook faults such books for never saying that one town hates the town next to it.
claims.source: David 'Zeb' Cook, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 2, 2025
claims.quote: this town hates this town over here

claims.claim: Cook says a published world is not created for yourself but for other players to take and use.
claims.source: David 'Zeb' Cook, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 2, 2025
claims.quote: You are not creating a world for yourself

claims.claim: Richard Green says a new setting book must make clear at once what kind of adventures take place in that world.
claims.source: Richard Green, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 2, 2025
claims.quote: needs to be super clear what kind of adventures take place

claims.claim: Baur's opening essay describes good campaign setting design as stacking as many boxes of dynamite as possible.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Guide to Worldbuilding p.12, quoted in a Gnome Stew review
claims.quote: to stack as many boxes of dynamite as possible

claims.claim: Mizer reports that Carbonell conceptualises tabletop role-playing games first and foremost as literary gametexts.
claims.source: Nicholas J. Mizer, 'The Role of the Cosmographer', International Journal of Role-playing 18, 2025
claims.quote: conceptualizing TRPGs as, first and foremost, “literary gametexts”

claims.claim: Mizer argues the role-playing game emerges as a set of practices only later codified in a gametext.
claims.source: Nicholas J. Mizer, 'The Role of the Cosmographer', International Journal of Role-playing 18, 2025
claims.quote: a set of practices which are only later codified

claims.claim: A reviewer says Dread Trident theorises the posthuman by centering the gametexts and gametools that create gameplay.
claims.source: Adrianna Burton, 'Book Review: Dread Trident', Analog Game Studies, 2022
claims.quote: centering the gametexts and gametools that create gameplay
